Welcome to George Carey Church of England Primary School
Thank you for showing an interest in George Carey Church of England Primary School’s website. We are located within the Rivergate Community Centre at the heart of the Barking Riverside development; an area which continues to grow. As such we are at the centre of this new, rich and diverse community.
Our Latest News
Wear Yellow Friday 9th October
Wear yellow to school on Friday 9th October and say hello as we celebrate 10 years of standing out, starting conversations, so no young person feels alone with their mental health. If you would like to donate, please use the link below https://fundraise.youngminds.org.uk/event/hello-yellow/donate
Jeans for Genes day
Friday 18th September is Jeans for Genes day. Your child can come to school wearing jeans. If you would like to make a donation, please visit the jeans for jeans website https://www.jeansforgenes.org/
Important Headteacher message
Important: School Snack and Lunchbox Arrangements from September 2026 Dear Parents and Carers, Following the introduction of the new statutory guidance on allergy safety in schools from September 2026, schools are required to take a whole-school approach to allergy management and reducing the risks associated with allergic reactions. The DFE guidance states that schools should take measures to manage the risks of exposure to allergen. This includes food brought in by others which includes parents, children and staff. Please understand that often children swap food and / or share, and it is very difficult to prevent this from happening. The consequences of a pupil eating or coming into contact with an allergen could be potentially fatal, and so we ask all families to adhere to our new rules. We have considered reasonable adjustments to reduce any risks of exposure to allergens. In order to reduce the risk of children being exposed unnecessarily to allergens, we are limiting the foods that the pupils can have access to during the school day. Break time snacks are limited to fresh or dried fruit only; which is healthy and not harmful to any of the pupils. We appreciate that this is a change for some families. The purpose of this approach is to provide a simple, consistent and healthy snack arrangement, while also helping the school to minimise unnecessary food allergens being brought into the school environment. Packed Lunch Boxes Please do not send children to school with: • Crisps • Biscuits • Nuts or nut products • Chocolate or sweets • Cakes or pastries • Cereal or snack bars • Other packaged or processed snacks Lunch boxes will be checked daily. It is vital that you label all packed lunch boxes with your child’s name and class. In this way we can ensure that children have access to their own lunch only and will not take an incorrect box. In the case of families preparing food for their children in lunchboxes, please be aware of potential allergens such as nuts as, once again, sometimes children attempt to share food (which we do not allow). We try as far as possible to ensure an ‘allergen free’ environment, but cannot guarantee this. We do not allow nuts onto our premises, but we are ‘nut aware’ rather than ‘nut free’, as children and families sometimes break this rule. Children with medical or dietary requirements We recognise that some children may require an alternative snack because of a medical condition, allergy or specific dietary requirement. Where this applies, please contact the school so that appropriate arrangements can be agreed in accordance with your child’s individual healthcare needs. No child will be disadvantaged as a result of a medically necessary dietary requirement. We ask all parents and carers to support us by ensuring that children only bring an appropriate and agreed snack to school. Thank you for your understanding and continued support in helping us to maintain a healthy, safe and inclusive environment for every child. Kind regards, Chris Harrison Headteacher

pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values Statement
At George Carey Church of England Primary School, we believe that fundamental British values are central to the provision that we offer at the school. To be a good citizen of the school children are encouraged to:
 Listen to others and tolerate those with different beliefs and values to their own
 Help others wherever possible
 Take responsibilities seriously
 Be kind to others and be charitable
 Look after the environment and the wider community
British values are taught explicitly through every aspect of provision, including through the curriculum, the activities that we undertake and through the school environment. British values are also reinforced through the school’s core Christian values of Love, Respect, Unity and Peace, which are prominently promoted throughout provision.
We promote the British values through:
 The school behaviour policy which sets out a framework of fairness and consistency which encourages children to understand the importance of the ‘rule of law.’ Golden Rules underpin the system, and these have been developed by the children themselves.
 Achievement and good behaviour is celebrated regularly and publically to the whole school community. The rewards system encourages children to develop in self?confidence, self-knowledge and self-esteem. Communication with parents about their children’s behaviour is effective and instant through our electronic ‘Dojo’ system; which allows parents to communicate and respond with ease.
 A strong pupil voice. The school council is well established and demonstrates to children the power that a democracy can have. Elections are held annually and children are asked to state what they believe in and what they would like to change about the school prior to the election. Council representative are in place from Years 1 to 6. The School Council have helped the school to improve overall provision and has given children a greater say in how the school runs. Pupil voice is also promoted and celebrated throughout the school environment, both in classrooms and in corridors on customised wallpapers.  Student Ambassadors are appointed at the end of Year 5 annually (interviewed by outgoing ambassadors leaving Year 6). The Ambassadors work in groups to share their experience and skills to improve selected aspects of school provision. Some of the most successful projects directed by the Ambassadors to date have involved improving the quality of playtimes, teaching younger children mathematics skills and developing the learning environment.
 The school curriculum focuses upon key events in history as well as key aspects of life in other countries. Children learn to respect the beliefs of others through the R.E. curriculum and excursions to other places of worship are part of our programme of educational visits programme. The spiritual, moral, social and cultural curriculum (SMSC) curriculum ensures that children’s experiences and understanding in these areas is developed as they move through the school.
 Special assemblies follow the Christian calendar and also focus upon key events which are culturally significant to Great Britain, such as St George’s Day, Bonfire Night, Remembrance Sunday, etc. Staff at George Carey Church of England Primary School are required to reflect the values of the school and provide a strong exemplar of the British values through the work that they do and the relationships that they demonstrate to others.

School Values
Our School
School Values
Aims and Core Values
Our new mission statement...
“A school for all with Jesus at the heart. Recognising the gift of every child, we work as one to enable them to become the person they were created to be”.
A team of staff governors and parents worked on refreshing our mission statement in the summer of 2022. The team looked at what the school represented and how this could be encompassed when also linked to the Schools' Core Values.
The theological route of this vision comes in Ephesians 4, v16:
"From him the whole body, joined and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love, as each part does its work."
The vision for the school is particularly relevant to the fact that we have a high proportion of high needs pupils and how we value all pupils. The children have a wide range of abilities and we value every child (recognising the gift each child brings). Our aim is to work together one body in order to achieve the best possible outcomes for the children.
An outstanding school where children enjoy, learning, achieve highly and enter into the next stage of their schooling with confidence ,
A place where children develop literacy, numeracy, creativity and communication skills necessary to fully access the curriculum and be successful throughout their lives.
A place where all children feel safe and protected; learning how to keep themselves and others safe.
A place where children develop in self-confidence, whilst understanding that this develops through risk taking and making mistakes.
A place where all children develop and grow within an inclusive environment which values and respects the difference between people.
A place where all children understand Christian values and are able to apply them to their everyday lives to after each other and contribute positively to the wider community.
A place where children will develop as citizens who belong to a community and who can thrive within a modern British society.
Our core Christian values are:-
We stand together as a school committed to positive and mutual support.
We have respect for all people of the world regardless of their religion, race, ability and sexual orientation.
We love and cherish the world and all God's creations contained within it.
We believe in peace between people and know that this is the route to happiness.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Our School
Welcome from the Headteacher
Thank you for showing an interest in George Carey Church of England Primary School’s website. We are located within the Rivergate Community Centre at the heart of the Barking Riverside development; an area which continues to grow. As such we are at the centre of this new, rich and diverse community.
The school opened in September 2011 and, in a short space of time, has grown into a full three form of entry school with a successful Nursery for 78 part time pupils. We follow the local authority’s admissions procedures and we do not select children based upon their ability or faith. Indeed, although we are a Church of England School we welcome pupils and staff from all religious backgrounds as well as those with none. The school is highly inclusive of children with additional needs and also incorporates an additional resource provision (ARP) for 12 children with Autistic Spectrum Disorders (ASD). Children are placed within this unit by the local authority through a referral process. ARP pupils join in with day to day school life and integrate into mainstream classes according to their individual levels of need.
At George Carey Church of England Primary School, children are at the heart of everything that we do. We pride ourselves in our child centred approaches and pupil voice is valued.
The school is flourishing and, if you are thinking of joining us, we look forward to sharing the experience and working with you in the drive for continued improvement.
Headteacher George Carey Church of England Primary School

pageCache.pageTitle: Reading VIPERS | George Carey Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reading VIPERS
Children are taught the skills of reading (outlined in the National Curriculum and the KS1 and KS2 test domains) through the use of VIPERS which were created by Rob Smith (The Literacy Shed).
The Reading Vipers can be used by both KS1 and KS2 with a little adaption. The main difference being in the S.
In KS1, ‘Explain’; is not one of the content domains, rather it asks children why they have come to a certain conclusion, to explain their preferences, thoughts and opinions about a text.
In KS2, the Explain section covers the additional content domains of 2F, 2G and 2H which are not present in KS1.
VIPERS is an anagram to aid the recall of the 6 reading domains as part of the UK’s reading curriculum. They are the key areas which we feel children need to know and understand in order to improve their comprehension of texts.
The 6 domains focus on the comprehension aspect of reading and not the mechanics: decoding, fluency, prosody etc. As such, VIPERS is not a reading scheme but rather a method of ensuring that teachers ask, and students are familiar with, a range of questions. They allow the teacher to track the type of questions asked and the children’s responses to these which allows for targeted questioning afterwards.
In Key Stage One children reading skills are taught and practised using the VIPERS during whole class reading sessions.
KS1 Content Domain Reference
1a draw on knowledge of vocabulary to understand texts
1b identify/ explain key aspects of fiction and non-fiction, such as characters, events, titles and information.
1c identify and explain the sequences of events in texts
1d make inferences from the text
1e predict what might happen on the basis of what has been read so far
In Key Stage Two children reading skills are taught and practised using VIPERS during whole class reading sessions.
KS2 Content Domain Reference
2a Give/explain the meaning of words in context
2b retrieve and record information/ identify key details from fiction and non/fiction
2c summarise main ideas from more than one paragraph
2d make inferences from the text/ explain and justify inferences with evidence from the text
2e predict what might happen from details stated or implied
2f identify/explain how information/ narrative content is related and contributes to meaning as a whole
2g identify/explain how meaning is enhanced through choice of words and phrases
2h make comparisons within a text

Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Personal, social and emotional development is one of the prime areas of learning within the EYFS. This area of development is divided into the following aspects:
-Building relationships
The EYFS statutory framework states "Children’s personal, social and emotional development (PSED) is crucial for children to lead healthy and happy lives, and is fundamental to their cognitive development. Underpinning their personal development are the important attachments that shape their social world. Strong, warm and supportive relationships with adults enable children to learn how to understand their own feelings and those of others. Children should be supported to manage emotions, develop a positive sense of self, set themselves simple goals, have confidence in their own abilities, to persist and wait for what they want and direct attention as necessary. Through adult modelling and guidance, they will learn how to look after their bodies, including healthy eating, and manage personal needs independently. Through supported interaction with other children, they learn how to make good friendships, co-operate and resolve conflicts peaceably. These attributes will provide a secure platform from which children can achieve at school and in later life." (DFE 2021)
In the EYFS, PSHE is taught weekly through our 'Jigsaw Scheme.' Through this scheme, children are taught a range of topics such as ' Being in my world, celebrating difference, dreams and goals, healthy me, relationships and changes.'
